extra.message: Affected versions of GitPython are vulnerable to Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'). An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by injecting newline characters into the value argument of GitPython config-writer methods (set_value, add_value), causing an attacker-controlled `[core] hooksPath=...` stanza to be written into `.git/config`. Subsequent Git operations that fire hooks (commit, merge, checkout, etc.) will then execute scripts from the attacker-controlled directory, leading to arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Affected versions of GitPython are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation. GitPython's `GitConfigParser` writer methods (`set_value`, `add_value`, `set`, `add_section`, `rename_section`) only sanitize the `value` argument for newline characters; the `section` and `option`/`new_name` arguments are passed through to `configparser` unvalidated. An attacker who controls one of those arguments can inject `\n[core]\nhooksPath=...` into `.git/config`, causing arbitrary code execution the next time any git hook runs. This bypasses the prior fix for CVE-2026-42215.

cwe: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation

extra.message: Affected versions of GitPython are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'). GitPython's `check_unsafe_options` validation runs before the underscore-to-hyphen normalization performed by `Git.transform_kwarg()`, so passing dangerous Git CLI flags (such as `--upload-pack`, `--receive-pack`, `--exec`, `--config`, `-c`, `-u`) as Python keyword arguments in their underscore form (e.g., `upload_pack="..."`, `receive_pack="..."`, `exec="..."`) bypasses the blocklist on the default `allow_unsafe_options=False` path. An attacker who can influence the keyword arguments forwarded to `Repo.clone`, `Repo.clone_from`, `Remote.fetch`, `Remote.pull`, or `Remote.push` can smuggle arbitrary commands into the resulting `git` invocation, leading to OS command injection.
